applies_why: Yes; this judge text is deciding a link collision involving the Isaiah 7:14 chain, so K-C's chain-versus-chain requirement governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'never verse by verse' in 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': I weighed whether a word-count that balances individual verses is a forbidden verse-by-verse method or a permissible lexical footing check; I read it as forbidden here because the rule says never verse by verse.
why: The judge resolves the Isaiah 7:14 link by treating the chapter-bound verses as real while saying the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, which is a verse/word-level weighing rather than a chain-against-chain footing comparison.
